Android 12 and later stop background processes they consider "phantom" — which includes the Linux programs a session runs. That makes sessions close suddenly, often in the middle of installing something.

AndLin can switch this off for you, once. It needs Wireless debugging for that: you will turn it on in Developer options and pair AndLin with your own device. AndLin then runs three settings commands:

• device_config set_sync_disabled_for_tests persistent
• device_config put activity_manager max_phantom_processes 2147483647
• settings put global settings_enable_monitor_phantom_procs false

You can turn Wireless debugging off again afterwards.
This Android version doesn\'t have Wireless debugging, so %1$s will be installed with the system installer. Allow AndLin to install apps if asked.

1. Open Developer options (if you don't have them, go to Settings › About phone and tap Build number seven times).
2. Turn on Wireless debugging. Your device must be on Wi-Fi.
3. Tap Wireless debugging, then "Pair device with pairing code".
4. Type the six-digit code into the notification from AndLin — or come back here and type it below.
